subproblems.title: Integrated convergence of blown-up difference quotients on a ball
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, F : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, L : ℝ^n → ℝ^P a continuous linear map, b ∈ ℝ^n, f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous with compact support, and R ∈ ℝ. Suppose F has Fréchet derivative L at b. Then ∫_{B̄_R(0)} |f(r^{-1}(F(b + rc) − F(b))) − f(Lc)| dλ(c) → 0 as r → 0⁺. Here λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n, B̄_R(0) = {c : |c| ≤ R}, the integral is a Bochner integral (equal to 0 by convention when the integrand is not integrable on B̄_R(0)), and no measurability of F is assumed.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (F : Euclid n → Euclid P) (L : Euclid n →L[ℝ] Euclid P) (b : Euclid n) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (R : ℝ), HasFDerivAt F L b → Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => ∫ c in closedBall (0 : Euclid n) R, ‖f (r⁻¹ • (F (b + r • c) - F b)) - f (L c)‖ ∂volume) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 8 of the parent proof (T₃ → 0). Here the ball radius R is an arbitrary real number and L is an arbitrary Fréchet derivative of F at b. In the parent, L = DF(b) and the radius is R_f/m.
Notation:
- λ := Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n and D := B̄_R(0);
- Φ_r(c) := r^{-1}(F(b + rc) − F(b)) and T(r) := ∫_D |f(Φ_r(c)) − f(Lc)| dλ(c);
- V := λ(D) as a real number and S := |R| + 1.
1. Preliminaries.
- D is closed and bounded in ℝ^n, hence compact, so λ(D) < ∞ (measure_closedBall_lt_top) and V ≥ 0.
- S > 0, and every c ∈ D satisfies |c| ≤ R ≤ |R| < S.
- For every r, T(r) ≥ 0 because it is the integral of a nonnegative function (integral_nonneg).
2. Let ε > 0 and put ε₁ := ε/(V + 1) > 0.
3. Uniform continuity. f is continuous with compact support, hence uniformly continuous (HasCompactSupport.uniformContinuous_of_continuous). So there is η > 0 with |f(w) − f(w')| < ε₁ whenever |w − w'| < η (Metric.uniformContinuous_iff).
4. Differentiability. Put θ := η/(2S) > 0.
- Since F has derivative L at b, F(b + k) − F(b) − Lk = o(|k|) as k → 0 (hasFDerivAt_iff_isLittleO_nhds_zero). So |F(b + k) − F(b) − Lk| ≤ θ|k| for all k in a neighbourhood of 0.
- Hence there is δ₀ > 0 with |F(b + k) − F(b) − Lk| ≤ θ|k| whenever |k| < δ₀ (Metric.eventually_nhds_iff).
5. Pointwise bound. Put δ := δ₀/S > 0, and let 0 < r < δ and c ∈ D.
- |rc| = r|c| < rS < δS = δ₀, using |c| < S, r > 0 and S > 0. So |F(b + rc) − F(b) − L(rc)| ≤ θ|rc| = θr|c|.
- L is linear, so L(rc) = rLc. Since r ≠ 0, Φ_r(c) − Lc = r^{-1}(F(b + rc) − F(b) − L(rc)).
- Therefore |Φ_r(c) − Lc| = r^{-1}|F(b + rc) − F(b) − L(rc)| ≤ θ|c| ≤ θS = η/2 < η.
- Step 3 then gives |f(Φ_r(c)) − f(Lc)| < ε₁.
6. Integral bound. Let 0 < r < δ.
- By step 5, the integrand of T(r) has absolute value at most ε₁ at every point of D, and λ(D) < ∞. So |T(r)| ≤ ε₁·V (norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const, which needs no measurability of the integrand).
- If the integrand is not integrable on D, then T(r) = 0 by the convention for Bochner integrals and this bound is immediate.
- With step 1, 0 ≤ T(r) ≤ ε₁V = εV/(V + 1) < ε.
7. Conclusion. For every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 with |T(r) − 0| < ε whenever 0 < r < δ. This is exactly T(r) → 0 as r → 0⁺ (Metric.tendsto_nhdsWithin_nhds, applied to the set (0, ∞) and the point 0).
proof_key_steps: Set D = B̄_R(0), V = λ(D) < ∞ and S = |R| + 1, so |c| < S on D; note T(r) ≥ 0.
Given ε > 0, uniform continuity of f gives η for ε₁ = ε/(V + 1).
Differentiability at b gives δ₀ with |F(b+k) − F(b) − Lk| ≤ (η/(2S))|k| whenever |k| < δ₀.
For 0 < r < δ₀/S and c ∈ D, |Φ_r(c) − Lc| ≤ η/2 < η, so the integrand is < ε₁.
Hence 0 ≤ T(r) ≤ ε₁V < ε, so T(r) → 0 as r → 0⁺.

subproblems.title: Averages of the complement indicator vanish at a density-one point
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, B ⊆ ℝ^n Borel and b ∈ ℝ^n. Suppose λ(B ∩ B̄_ρ(b))/λ(B̄_ρ(b)) → 1 as ρ → 0⁺, with the quotient taken in [0, ∞]. Then ⨍_{B̄_s(b)} 1_{ℝ^n∖B} dλ → 0 as s → 0⁺. Here λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n, and the averages are Bochner set averages of the real-valued indicator function of the complement of B.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (B : Set (Euclid n)) (b : Euclid n), MeasurableSet B → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => volume (B ∩ closedBall b ρ) / volume (closedBall b ρ)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1) → Tendsto (fun s : ℝ => ⨍ a in closedBall b s, Bᶜ.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) a ∂volume) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the first bullet of step 6 of the parent proof, which verifies the hypothesis of pit_integral_closedBall_rescale_tendsto for h = 1_{ℝ^n∖B}. Here it is stated on its own.
Notation:
- λ := Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n, and λ_ℝ(E) := λ(E) as a real number (toReal);
- for s > 0, C_s := B̄_s(b) and q(s) := λ(B ∩ C_s)/λ(C_s) ∈ [0, ∞].
1. Fix s > 0.
- C_s contains the nonempty open ball B_s(b), and Lebesgue measure is positive on nonempty open sets, so λ(C_s) > 0 (measure_closedBall_pos).
- C_s is compact, so λ(C_s) < ∞ (measure_closedBall_lt_top).
- Hence λ_ℝ(C_s) > 0.
2. ℝ^n∖B is Borel, so ∫_{C_s} 1_{ℝ^n∖B} dλ = ∫_{C_s ∩ (ℝ^n∖B)} 1 dλ = λ_ℝ(C_s ∖ B) (setIntegral_indicator, setIntegral_const).
3. B is Borel and λ(C_s) < ∞, so λ_ℝ(C_s ∩ B) + λ_ℝ(C_s ∖ B) = λ_ℝ(C_s) (measureReal_inter_add_sdiff). Hence ∫_{C_s} 1_{ℝ^n∖B} dλ = λ_ℝ(C_s) − λ_ℝ(B ∩ C_s).
4. By the definition of the set average (setAverage_eq) and λ_ℝ(C_s) ≠ 0 from step 1:
⨍_{C_s} 1_{ℝ^n∖B} dλ = λ_ℝ(C_s)^{-1}·(λ_ℝ(C_s) − λ_ℝ(B ∩ C_s)) = 1 − λ_ℝ(B ∩ C_s)/λ_ℝ(C_s).
5. In [0, ∞], (x/y).toReal = x.toReal/y.toReal (ENNReal.toReal_div), so q(s).toReal = λ_ℝ(B ∩ C_s)/λ_ℝ(C_s). Therefore, for every s > 0, ⨍_{B̄_s(b)} 1_{ℝ^n∖B} dλ = 1 − q(s).toReal.
6. By hypothesis q(s) → 1 as s → 0⁺. Since 1 ≠ ∞, toReal is continuous at 1 (ENNReal.tendsto_toReal). So q(s).toReal → 1, and 1 − q(s).toReal → 1 − 1 = 0.
7. The identity of step 5 holds for all s ∈ (0, ∞), and this set belongs to the filter 𝓝[>] 0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin). Functions that agree eventually have the same limit (Tendsto.congr'). So ⨍_{B̄_s(b)} 1_{ℝ^n∖B} dλ → 0 as s → 0⁺.
No case split on n is needed. For n = 0, ℝ^0 is a single point of measure 1, and the same computation applies.
proof_key_steps: ∫_{B̄_s(b)} 1_{Bᶜ} = λ_ℝ(B̄_s(b)) − λ_ℝ(B ∩ B̄_s(b)) by additivity, since B is Borel.
So for s > 0 the average equals 1 − (λ(B ∩ B̄_s(b))/λ(B̄_s(b))).toReal.
toReal is continuous at 1, so the averages tend to 1 − 1 = 0; transfer along the eventual identity on (0, ∞).

subproblems.title: Localised three-term estimate for the rescaled area integrals
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, F : ℝ^n → ℝ^P continuous, L : ℝ^n → ℝ^P continuous linear, B ⊆ ℝ^n Borel, J : ℝ^n → ℝ Borel with 0 ≤ J ≤ K, m > 0, b ∈ ℝ^n, f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous, and R, M, r ∈ ℝ. Assume (labels (i) and (iii) as in the parent) (i) m|a − b| ≤ |F(a) − F(b)| for all a ∈ B; (iii) m|c| ≤ |Lc| for all c ∈ ℝ^n; f(w) = 0 whenever |w| ≥ R; |f(w)| ≤ M for all w; and r > 0. Write Φ_r(c) := r^{-1}(F(b + rc) − F(b)) and D := B̄_{R/m}(0). Then |∫_{ℝ^n} 1_B(b + rc)·J(b + rc)·f(Φ_r(c)) dλ(c) − J(b)·∫_{ℝ^n} f(Lc) dλ(c)| ≤ KM·∫_D 1_{ℝ^n∖B}(b + rc) dλ(c) + M·∫_D |J(b + rc) − J(b)| dλ(c) + J(b)·∫_D |f(Φ_r(c)) − f(Lc)| dλ(c). Here λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n and all integrals are Bochner integrals.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (F : Euclid n → Euclid P) (L : Euclid n →L[ℝ] Euclid P) (B : Set (Euclid n)) (J : Euclid n → ℝ) (K m : ℝ) (b : Euclid n) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (R M r : ℝ), Continuous F → MeasurableSet B → Measurable J → (∀ a, 0 ≤ J a ∧ J a ≤ K) → 0 < m → (∀ a ∈ B, m * ‖a - b‖ ≤ ‖F a - F b‖) → (∀ c, m * ‖c‖ ≤ ‖L c‖) → Continuous f → (∀ w, R ≤ ‖w‖ → f w = 0) → (∀ w, ‖f w‖ ≤ M) → 0 < r → ‖(∫ c, B.indicator J (b + r • c) * f (r⁻¹ • (F (b + r • c) - F b)) ∂volume) - J b * (∫ c, f (L c) ∂volume)‖ ≤ K * M * (∫ c in closedBall (0 : Euclid n) (R / m), Bᶜ.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) (b + r • c) ∂volume) + M * (∫ c in closedBall (0 : Euclid n) (R / m), ‖J (b + r • c) - J b‖ ∂volume) + J b * (∫ c in closedBall (0 : Euclid n) (R / m), ‖f (r⁻¹ • (F (b + r • c) - F b)) - f (L c)‖ ∂volume)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–5 of the parent proof (setup, localisation, integrability, pointwise and integrated estimates) for one fixed r > 0. R and M are now hypotheses, and L is any continuous linear map satisfying (iii). In the parent, L = DF(b), R comes from HasCompactSupport.exists_pos_le_norm, and M from Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support.
Notation:
- λ := Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n, Φ_r(c) := r^{-1}(F(b + rc) − F(b)) and D := B̄_{R/m}(0);
- X(c) := 1_B(b + rc)·J(b + rc)·f(Φ_r(c)), i.e. B.indicator J (b + r•c) · f(Φ_r(c)), and Y(c) := J(b)·f(Lc);
- g₁(c) := 1_{ℝ^n∖B}(b + rc), g₂(c) := |J(b + rc) − J(b)| and g₃(c) := |f(Φ_r(c)) − f(Lc)|;
- G := KM·g₁ + M·g₂ + J(b)·g₃.
1. Constants. M ≥ |f(0)| ≥ 0 and 0 ≤ J(b) ≤ K, so K ≥ 0. D is a closed ball, so λ(D) < ∞ (measure_closedBall_lt_top).
2. Localisation. Let c ∉ D, i.e. |c| > R/m. As m > 0, R < m|c|.
- X(c) = 0. If b + rc ∉ B, the indicator factor is 0. If b + rc ∈ B, apply (i) with a := b + rc: m·r|c| = m|(b + rc) − b| ≤ |F(b + rc) − F(b)|. Since r > 0, |Φ_r(c)| = r^{-1}|F(b + rc) − F(b)| ≥ m|c| > R. So R ≤ |Φ_r(c)| and f(Φ_r(c)) = 0.
- Y(c) = 0. By (iii), |Lc| ≥ m|c| > R, so f(Lc) = 0.
- Hence ∫ X dλ = ∫_D X dλ and ∫ Y dλ = ∫_D Y dλ (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero). Also J(b)·∫ f(Lc) dλ(c) = ∫ Y dλ (integral_const_mul).
3. Measurability and bounds.
- c ↦ b + rc is continuous. B.indicator J is Borel because B and J are, so c ↦ B.indicator J (b + rc), g₁ and g₂ are Borel.
- c ↦ f(Φ_r(c)) and c ↦ f(Lc) are continuous because F, f and L are, so X, Y and g₃ are Borel.
- |B.indicator J (b + rc)| ≤ K, so |X| ≤ KM; also |Y| ≤ KM.
- 0 ≤ g₁ ≤ 1; 0 ≤ g₂ ≤ K because J(b + rc) and J(b) lie in [0, K]; 0 ≤ g₃ ≤ 2M.
4. Integrability. A bounded Borel function is integrable on a set of finite measure (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded). By steps 1 and 3, X, Y, g₁, g₂ and g₃ are integrable on D, hence so is G.
5. Pointwise estimate. Fix c and write u := f(Φ_r(c)) and v := f(Lc); then |u| ≤ M.
- If b + rc ∈ B: g₁(c) = 0 and X(c) − Y(c) = J(b + rc)u − J(b)v = (J(b + rc) − J(b))u + J(b)(u − v). So |X(c) − Y(c)| ≤ M·g₂(c) + J(b)·g₃(c) = G(c), using J(b) ≥ 0.
- If b + rc ∉ B: g₁(c) = 1 and X(c) = 0, so |X(c) − Y(c)| = |Y(c)| = J(b)|v| ≤ KM ≤ KM + M·g₂(c) + J(b)·g₃(c) = G(c). This uses 0 ≤ J(b) ≤ K, |v| ≤ M, M·g₂(c) ≥ 0 and J(b)·g₃(c) ≥ 0.
- So |X(c) − Y(c)| ≤ G(c) for every c.
6. Integrated estimate.
- By steps 2 and 4, ∫ X dλ − J(b)·∫ f(Lc) dλ(c) = ∫_D X dλ − ∫_D Y dλ = ∫_D (X − Y) dλ (integral_sub).
- By step 5 and the integrability of G on D, |∫_D (X − Y) dλ| ≤ ∫_D G dλ (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le).
- By linearity and step 4 (integral_add, integral_const_mul), ∫_D G dλ = KM·∫_D g₁ dλ + M·∫_D g₂ dλ + J(b)·∫_D g₃ dλ.
Combining these three facts gives exactly the claimed inequality.
proof_key_steps: Constants: M ≥ 0, 0 ≤ J(b) ≤ K and λ(D) < ∞ for D = B̄_{R/m}(0).
Localisation: by (i), (iii) and f = 0 off the open R-ball, X and Y vanish off D, so both integrals reduce to D.
All integrands are bounded Borel functions, hence integrable on D.
Pointwise: |X − Y| ≤ KM·g₁ + M·g₂ + J(b)·g₃, by cases on b + rc ∈ B.
Integrate over D: |∫X − J(b)∫f∘L| = |∫_D (X − Y)| ≤ ∫_D G = KM∫_D g₁ + M∫_D g₂ + J(b)∫_D g₃.
